cards.explanation: The answer is the man who fears the LORD, friends. The psalm says, "Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments." (Psalm 112:1) Notice who gets the blessing. The psalm names the man who fears the LORD.

The answer is delights, friends! The psalm says the man who fears the LORD "…greatly delights in His commandments." (Psalm 112:1) Not puts up with them, not squints at them. He delights. That's the face of someone who loves what he's been given.
The answer is True, friends. The psalm says, "His descendants will be mighty in the land…" (Psalm 112:2) The blessing doesn't stop with him. It reaches past him to the ones who come after.

The answer is True, friends! The psalm says, "…his righteousness endures forever." (Psalm 112:3) Wealth and riches sit in his house, but the righteousness is the part that never runs out. Nobody has to check the pantry for that one.

The answer is that light dawns for them, friends. The psalm says, "Light dawns in the darkness for the upright…" (Psalm 112:4) I know a little about dark places, and when light shows up in one, you never forget it. This light is for the gracious, compassionate and righteous.

The answer is the man who is generous and lends freely, friends. The psalm says, "It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice." (Psalm 112:5) He gives and lends without clutching his purse. And the psalm says it is well with him.

The answer is False, friends. The psalm says, "Surely he will never be shaken…" (Psalm 112:6) Not shaken now, not shaken later. And it adds that "the righteous man will be remembered forever." (Psalm 112:6)

The answer is that his heart trusts in the LORD, friends. The psalm says, "He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD." (Psalm 112:7) The psalm doesn't say he knows the news ahead of time. It says his heart is trusting in the LORD.
The answer is the poor, friends. The psalm says, "He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor…" (Psalm 112:9) Scattered, like seed tossed out by the handful. This man gives his gifts wide.

The answer is that he will be grieved and gnash his teeth, friends. The psalm says, "The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away…" (Psalm 112:10) It's a heavy ending for him. The psalm closes by saying, "the desires of the wicked will perish." (Psalm 112:10)
